x-handover.name: model predictions and recommendations
x-handover.source: Anil Wipat, bioprospecting use case slides, dbtl-synbio/dbtlhub, 10 Nov 2026
x-handover.note: The use case numbers its handovers. Carrying that number in the contract means two teams arguing about 'the Design handover' are provably arguing about the same one.

title: Learn -> Design handover (generic)
description: The handover that closes the cycle. Learn has fitted a model to the screening results and now proposes what Design should make next. The receiving phase cannot act on a ranked list alone: it needs to know which measurements each recommendation rests on, which model produced it and on what data, and how uncertain the prediction is. A point prediction with no uncertainty cannot be used to choose between candidates, so this contract refuses one.

profile.description: Which use-case profile this package was written against.

produced_by.description: 'engine' records the model used for the agent's own decisions, or 'none' for a deterministic step. It is not the scientific model - that is 'model' below, and the two must not be confused.

test_ref.description: MANDATORY: the Test -> Learn package this round learned from. A recommendation that cannot be traced to the measurements behind it is an opinion, and Design has no way to weigh it against the next one.

results.description: The result identifiers that were available to the model. Recommendations cite these.

model.description: What produced the predictions. Without a version and a training set a prediction cannot be reproduced, cannot be audited, and cannot be compared with the next round's - which makes the whole cycle unmeasurable.

version.description: A released version, a commit, or a content hash. 'latest' is not a version.

trained_on.description: The run_ids whose results the model was fitted on. More than one once the cycle has turned.

holdout.description: Optional but strongly wanted: how the model was checked against data it had not seen.

recommendations.description: What Design should make next round, in the order Learn would make them.

rank.description: Learn's own ordering. Design may ignore it, but it must be stated rather than implied by array position.

proposes.description: What to make. Either a change to something already built, or a new candidate - and in both cases it has to be a thing a Design agent can act on, not a sentence.

derived_from_design_item.description: Required when kind is variant_of or repeat_with_change.

change.description: What to change, stated precisely enough to build: a substitution, a promoter swap, a condition.

sequence.description: For a new candidate: the sequence itself, not a description of it.

evidence.description: The result identifiers from test_ref that this recommendation rests on. Not decoration: it is what lets Design see whether two recommendations are independent or are the same observation twice.

predictions.description: What the model expects, in the same measurement shape as every other handover - with uncertainty required, because a point prediction cannot be used to choose.

unit.description: Use 'dimensionless' rather than omitting the field; 'none' is not a unit.

method.description: The model and the procedure, e.g. 'ESM-2 + MLP, 5-fold CV mean'.

uncertainty.description: REQUIRED in this handover, unlike the others. A ranked list of point estimates tells Design nothing about where to spend a plate.

kind.description: What the number is. 'error bar' is not an answer.

in_training_range.description: Whether the prediction is an interpolation or an extrapolation. Design is allowed to accept an extrapolation; it is not allowed to be unaware it made one.

reads.description: Crates or packages this handover READ but did not produce. Information in this framework normally flows one way, from the phase that made something to the phase that receives it. This is the other direction: a receiving phase states what it can do, and the sending phase has to have looked. Referenced, never inlined - the package stays small and the graph joins the crates by their identifiers.

role.description: constraints: limits this package had to respect. context: read to interpret something. upstream: where the material came from.

checksum.description: Which version was read. A shared crate grows between rounds, so 'the Build crate' is not a unique thing to have read.

limits.description: Limits this package was built to respect, lifted out of the crates named in 'reads'. Carried here rather than left in the crate so that a check can compare against them, and 'from' says which crate each one came out of. A limit is not a use-case constant and does not belong in the profile: it is this run's equipment and this round's budget, and it changes between rounds.

from.description: The crate this limit was read out of.

stated_by.description: Who or what put it there - a researcher seeding the crate before round 1, or a phase recording its own equipment.

x-dbtl-checks.fix_hint: not auto-fixable: renaming one of them hides the collision instead of resolving it, and the two may not be the same recommendation

x-dbtl-checks.message: two recommendations claim the same rank
x-dbtl-checks.fix_hint: not auto-fixable: the ordering is Learn's judgement. Resolving a tie by array position would invent a preference nobody expressed

x-dbtl-checks.message: this recommendation cites a result that is not in the data it claims to have learned from
x-dbtl-checks.fix_hint: not auto-fixable: a recommendation whose evidence cannot be found is not traceable to any measurement. Either the result is added to test_ref, or the recommendation is withdrawn

x-dbtl-checks.message: proposes a variant of something that was never built and measured this round
x-dbtl-checks.fix_hint: not auto-fixable: either the item belongs in test_ref, or the recommendation is a new candidate and should say so
not auto-fixable: a quantity the model did not predict cannot be supplied. Either the model is asked for it, or the recommendation is reported as incomplete
